title: Disambiguation picker for ambiguous short IDs (CLI + console)
description:
# Disambiguation picker for ambiguous short IDs (CLI + console)

## Problem

With the dynamic short ID default of 4 characters (epic: kbs-429fa3), prefix collisions become routine at board sizes of a few hundred issues. Today every resolver reacts differently: Rust's `resolve_issue_identifier` (rust/src/issue_creation.rs) fails with a bare "ambiguous short id" and no candidates, Python's `issue_lookup.py` lists matches, and the console returns "issue id is ambiguous" as a 400 in `rust/src/bin/console_local.rs` and a dead-end error in `resolveIssueByIdentifier` (apps/console/src/App.tsx). We need one consistent recovery path: a disambiguation picker.

## Scope

Every command that resolves a user-supplied issue identifier through the shared resolver: `show`, `update`, `close`, `comment` (and `comment update` / `comment delete`), `delete`, `move`, `dep add` / `dep remove`, `create` / `update` with `--parent <prefix>`, `now <id>`, and so on. Not just `kbs show`.

## Resolver contract (Rust + Python)

Resolvers return a shared result type instead of a bare error:

- `Resolved(full_id)`
- `NotFound`
- `Ambiguous { candidate, matches: Vec<IssueSummary> }` where `IssueSummary = { id, key, type, status, title, project }`
  - `id` is the full stored ID; `key` is the display key produced by the ID list formatter run over the match set.

Rust `resolve_issue_identifier` (rust/src/issue_creation.rs, currently "ambiguous short id" with no candidate list at line 270) and the Python resolvers (`python/src/kanbus/issue_lookup.py`, `issue_creation.py`) converge on the same shape and the same human-readable text. The interactive prompt lives in the CLI layer only; libraries and the console backend consume `Ambiguous` structurally.

## CLI behavior

### Interactive TTY

When stdin and stdout are TTYs (`std::io::IsTerminal` in Rust, `sys.stdin.isatty()` in Python), and `--json` is not set, the CLI prints an indexed menu instead of failing:

```
"kbs-60bf" is ambiguous; 2 issues match:

  1) kbs-60bfa3  [task, in_progress]  Fix drag-and-drop on Safari   (Kanbus)
  2) kbs-60bfc1  [bug, open]         Console 400 on ambiguous id   (Kanbus)

Select 1-2, or press Enter to cancel:
```

- Candidate keys come from the ID list formatter applied to the match set: guaranteed mutually unique and minimal, and by construction wider than the ambiguous prefix, so every row can be copy-pasted straight back into a command.
- Rows show: formatted key, type, status, title, project label (on multi-project boards).
- A number selection proceeds with the chosen full ID and prints one confirmation line, e.g. `Resolved kbs-60bf -> kbs-60bfa3  ("Fix drag-and-drop on Safari")`.
- Enter with no selection cancels and exits with the same exit code as the non-interactive error, so wrappers around a TTY session see consistent behavior.

### Non-interactive / agents

Never prompt when there is no TTY, when `--json` is set, or when `KANBUS_NO_PROMPT=1` (also exposed as a `--no-prompt` flag).

Text output is a structured error followed by the same candidate rows:

```
error: ambiguous short id "kbs-60bf"; 2 issues match:
  kbs-60bfa3  [task, in_progress]  Fix drag-and-drop on Safari   (Kanbus)
  kbs-60bfc1  [bug, open]         Console 400 on ambiguous id   (Kanbus)
Re-run with one of the full IDs above.
```

JSON output (`--json`):

```json
{
  "error": "ambiguous_identifier",
  "candidate": "kbs-60bf",
  "matches": [
    {
      "id": "kbs-60bfa390-11aa-4bbb-8ccc-ddddeeeeffff",
      "key": "kbs-60bfa3",
      "type": "task",
      "status": "in_progress",
      "title": "Fix drag-and-drop on Safari",
      "project": "Kanbus"
    }
  ]
}
```

Full IDs in `matches[].id` (JSON output keeps full IDs); `key` is the formatter-derived display form for convenience.

**Exit code:** stable dedicated exit code 3 for `ambiguous_identifier`. Only 1 and 2 are used today (rust/src/main.rs maps `KanbusError::CommandFailure { exit_code }`; cli.rs:1816 and router.rs use 2), so 3 is free. Implement via the existing `CommandFailure { exit_code }` mechanism (rust/src/error.rs:34) and mirror in Python. Document in CLI_REFERENCE.md.

**Agent retry contract** (documented in CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md): on exit code 3 / `ambiguous_identifier`, re-run once with the full `id` from `matches`. Never guess a longer prefix. For scripted work, start from `--json` output (full IDs) and the round-trip never happens. Token note: one ambiguity retry costs more than the two characters the 4-char default saves per ID, so agents performing many ID operations should prefer JSON mode.

## Console behavior

### API

- `find_issue_matches` (rust/src/console_backend.rs) and the `console_local.rs` handlers that today return 400 "issue id is ambiguous" (~7 sites: lines 642, 668, 781, 827, 867, 1028, 1068) instead return **HTTP 409** with:

```json
{ "error": "ambiguous_identifier", "candidate": "kbs-60bf", "matches": [ { "id": "...", "key": "kbs-60bfa3", "type": "task", "status": "in_progress", "title": "...", "project": "Kanbus" } ] }
```

- 404 stays "not found"; 409 is the resolvable state. API consumers (scripts, agents) always get full IDs in `matches`.

### UI

- `resolveIssueByIdentifier` (apps/console/src/App.tsx) returns `{ matches }` for the ambiguous case instead of `{ error: "Issue id is ambiguous" }`.
- A modal picker lists candidates with keys from the TS ID list formatter (kbs-c118a7): key, title, type badge, status, project.
- Keyboard navigation: Up/Down to move, Enter to open, Esc to dismiss and stay on the current route. Optional type-to-filter within the modal.
- Selecting a candidate navigates to `${basePath}/issues/${fullId}/` — URLs keep full IDs exactly as today (App.tsx already builds URLs from `resolved.issue.id`).
- A short ID in a URL that has become ambiguous renders the same modal; no new URL state (a refresh re-prompts if it is still ambiguous).
- Other console views that resolve identifiers (search, focus, deep links) route through the same picker component.

## Interaction with the ID list formatter and the matcher

- The picker's candidate keys are the ID list formatter applied to the candidate list — the same "widen only the colliding group" logic — so the picker is the formatter's first consumer and its natural test vehicle.
- Hyphen-insensitive matching is a prerequisite: candidates must be found by comparing hyphen-stripped prefixes so IDs widened past 8 characters (beyond the UUID's first internal hyphen) resolve. The fix applies to `issue_identifier_matches` (rust/src/ids.rs), `matches_issue_identifier` (python/src/kanbus/ids.py), `short_id_matches` (rust/src/console_backend.rs:291 — not just removing the `> 6` cap), and `shortIdMatches` (apps/console/src/App.tsx:424).
- Dotted sub-IDs compare base and suffix separately, so `kbs-abc1234.2` resolves against the full `kbs-abc1234567….2`.

## Testing

- Gherkin (shared Rust + Python harnesses): ambiguous candidate in non-TTY mode produces the structured error; TTY mode renders the menu (driven with piped stdin); JSON mode produces the payload; exit code 3 in both languages; console 409 payload shape.
- Property tests: for random UUID sets, every ambiguous group's formatted candidate keys are unique, and each candidate key is wider than the ambiguous input prefix.
- Fixtures: 4-char collision pair; local-vs-shared same-key collision; dotted sub-ID collision; widened-past-8 (hyphen) case; beads-mode IDs; numeric-only IDs.
